A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLTT research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching the renumbered theoretical analysis and qualitative examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original RLTT training experiments, benchmark evaluations, statistical tests, ablations, and qualitative comparisons using Ouro-2.6B-Thinking.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds Ouro-1.4B evaluations, AIME26 results, trained Qwen3 baselines, and compute-cost and representation analyses.

M1.justification: Equations 1–9 and Algorithm 1 retain the same trajectory-weighted objective, group-normalized advantages, terminal-loop KL regularization, sampling procedure, and three weighting strategies. Testing another Ouro size does not change the method.

E1.justification: v3 adds AIME26 evaluation in Section 5.2 and Tables 2 and 4. MATH training and all eight existing evaluation benchmarks remain, making this a limited extension of mathematical task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B trained with GRPO, whereas v1 evaluated their original checkpoints only. It removes Ouro-2.6B+SFT from the main comparison, although SFT remains in appendix Tables 3 and 9. This substantially strengthens the non-looped RL comparison while changing main-table comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix A.2 increase GRPO's MATH-500/GSM8K decoding budgets from 2048/512 to 3072 tokens, while retaining RLTT's 2048/512 budgets. v3 also adds Ouro-1.4B experiments and a CKA protocol using 30 AIME26 prompts with four loops. These materially change comparison conditions and extend the evaluation design.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.8 examines inference-compute trade-offs against Qwen3, and new A.9 tests premature representation collapse using CKA. These address two previously untested questions. Existing decode-budget, weighting, Pass@k, loop-depth, GSNR, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report evaluations using 10 inference seeds, temperature 0.2, paired t-tests at p < 0.05, and mean-plus/minus variation in Appendix A.2. Existing timing and GSNR statistical procedures also remain. Additional result rows and changed significance outcomes do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Substantial new results cover AIME26, Ouro-1.4B, and Qwen3+GRPO. Table 2 replaces 2.6B GRPO's MATH-500/GSM8K scores of 71.6/59.7 with 79.0/93.9 under longer budgets; RLTT remains 86.0/94.0. The 79.0 MATH-500 result already appeared in v1 Table 3. Appendix A.2 now reports significant gains on 8/9 benchmarks at 2.6B and 7/9 at 1.4B, versus v1's 8/8. Tables 11–12 add FLOPs and CKA findings.

T1.justification: Appendix A.8 becomes A.10 without changing Assumptions A.1–A.3, Lemma A.4, Theorem A.5, or their proofs. Section 6.1 restates previously available assumptions. The CKA formula documents a standard empirical metric rather than adding a theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract extends the quantified performance claim from Ouro-2.6B to both 1.4B and 2.6B, reporting mean gains of 5.8 and 10.9 percentage points over MATH-500, AIME24/26, and BeyondAIME. The introduction replaces its previous average-gain figures with a general consistent-gains claim. The central method, token-efficiency, and transfer contributions remain.

C2.justification: Appendix A.8 newly qualifies comparisons with Qwen3 as a compute–accuracy trade-off, reporting higher per-token FLOPs for Ouro. A.9 interprets CKA trends as progressive refinement rather than premature collapse. These add meaningful qualifications and mechanism discussion without replacing the existing interpretation or memory and adaptive-halting limitations.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository address, Qwen3+GRPO training details including a learning rate of 1e-4, explicit decoding budgets for the retained Pass@k analysis, and CKA representation-extraction details. Existing Ouro training hyperparameters and hardware disclosures are largely unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for MathArena, Loopformer, and CKA. The related-work discussion and central positioning remain largely unchanged. LSRL's updated publication entry represents the same previously cited work, not a newly introduced comparator.

P1.justification: The abstract and experimental discussion receive localized revisions, Section 6.1 expands its explanation using existing appendix assumptions, and two appendix sections are inserted before the renumbered theory and examples. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact; publication and acknowledgment text also change.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 4 expand with AIME26 and additional model groups, and new Tables 11 and 12 display compute-cost and CKA results. Captions and surrounding layout adjust, but Figures 1–6 retain identical artwork and the overall visual design remains stable.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, longer GRPO budgets and trained Qwen3 baselines make the comparisons more informative, while the second Ouro scale and compute/CKA analyses strengthen empirical assessment. However, v3 still claims matched inference conditions despite unequal budgets, and Section 5.2 claims significance on all 2.6B math benchmarks although Table 4 shows no GSM8K gain. These reporting inconsistencies limit the overall improvement.
